correctness.rationale: For globally finite-variation real data, Stieltjes integration gives the exact norm as the supremum of phi(t)He_{n-1}(t)/sqrt(n!). A first-order Hermite derivative identity and the exact energy derivative -2x(y')^2/n prove central/innermost-root global maxima. The even root perturbation follows from z''+(s/n)z'+z=0 with fixed initial data and variation of constants; the odd formula and both subleading terms follow from the central-binomial Stirling expansion. The necessary class explicitly allows half-line steps, avoiding a false finite-Lebesgue-L1 attainment premise. Exact integer recurrences and independent root/asymptotic computations in the included verifier passed. Asymptotic remainder is analytical, not deduced from finite tests.

value.rationale: The global-variation class is a natural nonsmooth input model for Gaussian orthogonal-polynomial coefficients. The exact norm and complete maximizing-jump localization determine the worst discontinuity for every Hermite degree; the nontrivial common n^-3/4 sharp scale plus explicitly opposite n^-1 parity corrections quantify the two distinct central oscillation mechanisms. These are structural all-degree results, not a one-off table entry or a routine reparameterization of the turning-point maximum of Krasikov.
